title: 2023 Tech Trends Report (16th edition)
author: Amy Webb (CEO, Future Today Institute)
notes: Partial. The 2023 edition was published as 14 separate volume PDFs plus an executive summary; no single full-report PDF was found in the Wayback Machine. Six volumes are archived complete and extracted here (Bioengineering, Climate & Energy, Health Care & Medicine, Metaverse, News & Information, Web3). The Artificial Intelligence volume capture is truncated (1 MB of the file) and unreadable; the other seven volumes were not found. Labels are the regular-weight entries of each volume table of contents, in printed order; medium-weight entries are sub-sections, bold entries are sections. Scenario questions (What if ...) and front/back matter are excluded. The executive summary lists no trend titles.

entries.subject: TPV Batteries

entries.label: Grid-Scale Energy Storage

entries.subject: Synthetic Health Data

entries.label: Patient Access to Medical Data
entries.quote: Americans are legally able to access their medical data, though existing systems make it difficult to access most of it.

entries.label: Automatic Medical Transcribing

entries.label: Remote Patient Monitoring

entries.label: Telemedicine

entries.quote: Big Tech is doubling down on its bid to muscle into the health care industry, while reorganizing and shifting strategies to take advantage of emerging technology breakthroughs.

entries.quote: From treatment of mental disorders to pain management, virtual reality is gaining traction in medicine.

entries.quote: In June 2022, doctors at Mount Sinai West in New York wired a patient’s brain with a 1.5-inch long implant created by Synchron, a brain-computer interface (BCI) startup.

entries.label: Bionic Noses

entries.quote: Neuroprosthetics exist for vision and hearing loss, but until recently there wasn’t a solution for the loss of other senses.

entries.quote: It’s now possible to remotely control fruit flies with a computer and command them to make specific movements.

entries.quote: Meta sponsored research at University of California, San Francisco, only to later abandon efforts to turn its BCI—which had the goal of allowing mobile device and computer users to communicate at a speed of at least 100 words per minute, much faster than anyone can type on a keyboard—into wearable consumer technology.

entries.quote: As wearables and sensor technology proliferate, so do floods of patient data that can help health care providers assess a person’s overall health.

entries.quote: Brain training is a controversial multibillion-dollar industry.

entries.quote: A team of researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems has designed and built a tiny millipede-like robot that can climb around in the gut to deliver therapeutic drugs.

entries.label: Nerve Coolers
entries.subsection: Health Care & Medicine Trends / Emerging Treatments
entries.quote: In 2022, researchers published a new breakthrough in managing pain.
entries.subject: Nerve Coolers

entries.label: Smart Materials

entries.quote: Nanowear’s SimpleSense is an FDA-cleared, noninvasive undergarment that monitors and analyzes multiple patient vitals—such as heart rate and sounds, respiration rate, lung volume, and physical activity—to predict risk of heart failure or lung disease, among other ailments.

entries.label: Diagnostic Beds
entries.subsection: Health Care & Medicine Trends / Emerging Diagnostics
entries.quote: Smart beds monitor patients’ breathing, temperature, pulse, and other vitals through sensor chips.

entries.label: Illness-Detecting Sensors

entries.quote: Researchers at the University of Waterloo in Canada are using computer vision and deep learning to create more natural movement for disabled persons who wear exoskeletons.
entries.subject: Assistive Exoskeletons

entries.label: Tattoos and Electronic Skins

entries.quote: The University of Texas at Austin is exploring how graphene electronic tattoos can measure brain waves, heart activity, and muscle activity through biopotentials, which are electrical activities naturally occurring in the body.
entries.subject: Tattoos and Electronic Skins

entries.label: Dissolving Bioelectronics

entries.subject: Ultrasound Stickers

entries.label: In-Ear EEG Devices
entries.subsection: Health Care & Medicine Trends / Emerging Wearables

entries.quote: Smartwatches are monitoring more than heart rates.

entries.quote: Scientists from MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory and Massachusetts General Hospital’s Center for Artificial Intelligence created an open-source toolkit that lets users design and fabricate health-sensing devices like bracelets that detect distracted driving or bands that provide important data during physical therapy like muscle motion, strain, and tension.

entries.quote: Head-mounted displays (HMDs), which offer more robust, immersive functionality than smart glasses but are too cumbersome and restrictive for casual use on the go, are more commonly worn in controlled workplace environments or for relatively stationary entertainment and gaming.

entries.quote: Avatars can be created in a variety of forms, but as users spend more time in XR and metaverse platforms virtually carrying out everyday tasks and interactions, there will be rising demand for avatars that can convincingly re-create their true human likeness.

entries.subsection: Trends / Digital Identities, Synthetic Media, and Generative AI
entries.quote: Founded in 2017, the personalized greeting app Cameo has made a name for itself by connecting public figures of varying levels of fame to average individuals—pay a fee, and the celeb (or B-lister) will record and deliver a personalized message to the recipient, whether it be a birthday greeting, a pep talk, or an apology on behalf of the sender.

entries.label: Synthetic Media in the Classroom and Workplace

entries.quote: Experiments in the metaverse are not without material brand reputation and consumer risk.

entries.subject: Deepfake Regulation and Synthetic Media Literacy

entries.quote: High-profile generative AI launches from OpenAI’s DALL-E and ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion’s text-to-image generator have raised thorny questions about fair use.

entries.label: Truth Decay in an Era of Synthetic Media
entries.quote: With the advent of synthetic media comes the end of the premise that seeing (or hearing) is believing.
entries.subject: Truth Decay in an Era of Synthetic Media

entries.label: Deepfake Detection
entries.quote: Last year, a viral synthetic video surfaced in which Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky appeared to tell his troops to surrender, but clues in the video—his head was oversized and his accent was flawed—got it quickly removed from distribution platforms.
entries.subject: Deepfake Detection

entries.label: Immersive Rights and Privacy in the Metaverse
entries.quote: Just as the internet continues to buck traditional jurisdictional boundaries, raising thorny legal questions about platform accountability and data rights, the metaverse and XR technologies will most certainly raise new questions that stretch the limits of legal precedent and analogy.
entries.subject: Immersive Rights and Privacy in the Metaverse

entries.label: Computer-Directed Reporting
entries.quote: A growing number of newsrooms are using AI-powered tools to automate tasks like homepage curation and initial drafting of breaking news stories.
entries.subject: Computer-Directed Reporting

entries.label: Dateline: Metaverse
entries.quote: News organizations should prepare to cover newsworthy events happening in persistent virtual spaces.
entries.subject: Dateline: Metaverse

entries.label: Digital Threat Modeling
entries.quote: Journalists are increasingly targeted by governments and other bad actors looking to discredit the media, influence stories, and gather intelligence.
entries.subject: Digital Threat Modeling

entries.label: Evolving Search Interfaces
entries.quote: Search engines are the gatekeepers for publishers and retailers looking to reach new audiences.
entries.subject: Evolving Search Interfaces

entries.label: Subscription Economy Matures
entries.quote: Subscriptions power multibillion-dollar media giants like The New York Times and individual passion projects on Substack alike.
entries.subject: Subscription Economy Matures

entries.label: Eroding Trust in News Organizations
entries.quote: Trust in news continues to fall, across continents and distribution channels.
entries.subject: Eroding Trust in News Organizations

entries.label: One-to-Few Networks.
entries.quote: Creating a personal media brand has never been easier.
entries.subject: One-to-Few Networks.

entries.label: Digital Frailty

entries.label: Sensory Journalism
entries.quote: Sensory journalism is storytelling that integrates directly with a consumer’s senses—either through an immersive experience using a virtual reality headset, or emerging devices like smart glasses or headphones that can augment a user’s perception.

entries.label: Teaching News Literacy
entries.quote: Not all of the information available is reliable.
entries.subject: Teaching News Literacy

entries.label: Policing the Creator Economy
entries.quote: The lifeblood of the content economy is ad revenue that creators can earn for delivering captive audiences to platforms.
entries.subject: Policing the Creator Economy

entries.label: Investigating Technology
entries.quote: As AI-powered decisions seep into every aspect of our lives, journalists need the skills and resources to hold algorithms—and the companies that design them— accountable.
entries.subject: Investigating Technology

entries.label: Media Consolidation
entries.quote: A handful of conglomerates own and influence the mainstream digital and print publishers in the US.
entries.subject: Media Consolidation

entries.label: Digital Redlining
entries.quote: Whether an individual can fully participate in the digital world—seeking news, building community, and accessing the myriad of services that depend on an internet connection—depends on where they are.
entries.subject: Digital Redlining

entries.label: Attention Metrics
entries.quote: Attention metrics go beyond just reach to measure whether consumers are engaging with content.

entries.label: User-Direct Media Formats

entries.subject: User-Direct Media Formats

entries.label: Rising Foundational Security Concerns

entries.label: Personal Distributed Computing Earning Models

entries.subject: Scaled NFT Utility

entries.label: Tools to Manage Digital Identity and Assets
entries.quote: The need for individuals to access, share, and prove their identity and store personal data and information is growing as digital interactions and transactions become increasingly common.
entries.subject: Tools to Manage Digital Identity and Assets

entries.label: Web 3-Enabled Health Care Enhancements
entries.quote: The health care industry, which underwent significant digitalization over the past decade, is facing positive disruption from Web3 technologies.

entries.quote: Web3 is being used to track, exchange, and archive intangible information for the first time, including cultural material, records of historically significant events, connections among people or organizations, and the scale of information sharing.
